notes: Summary: mid-market product analytics company evaluating Hosted -> Dedicated. Primary driver: predictable per-token costs during Q4 product launch + stricter data residency.
Use-case specifics: customer-facing support bot (chat) + embeddings for fast semantic search across product docs + reranking for feature recommendations.
Perf targets: 95th pctp latency <200ms for short chat queries (<=256 tokens), sustained throughput ~120 requests/sec at peak, burst to 360 req/sec for launch windows.
Cost sensitivity: wants committed baseline to get a predictable unit price; open to multi-tier ramp (3-month ramp to full commit).

Model preferences: prefer open/quantized model variants for cost (70B quant candidates) but need Redwood to validate latency on Dedicated GPUs; fallback to hosted smaller model if capacity constrained.
Security ask: must support SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, per-route audit logs, KMS integration for customer keys, and EU data residency for subset of data (user PII).
POC plan (engineering): 3-week Dedicated POC in VPC with sample traffic replay. Milestones: network peering, model validation <250ms 95th, KV/prefix cache check, cost telemetry export.

Pricing negotiation points: 1) baseline commit (tokens/month) vs unit price, 2) burst capacity (x3) pricing and guaranteed ramp windows, 3) overage pricing floor, 4) ramp schedule with credit offsets for early scaling.

AE notes from 2026-03-02 workshop: "We need a 6-9 month commitment but want a strong ramp schedule—first 3 months at 40% commit, month 4-6 at 75%, then full." Finance asked for blended per-token rate for first 6 months.
SE note: baseline sizing appears to map to 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for model variant but will test quantized kernels on Dedicated; estimate latency headroom ~20-30% before needing larger instances.
Legal ask: add explicit data residency clause, SLA for uptime 99.9% and latency SLOs, and a clause for overage reconciliation monthly.
decision_criteria: meets latency SLOs on Dedicated during peak
